recipes.label: Request ally reinforcements
recipes.startdescription:
Send word over wire and wave. If we need more manpower, this is the way to ask for it.

[This will consume one charge and summon several local fighter jets.]

recipes.label: Send an ally to procure reinforcements
recipes.startdescription:
With our communications non-operational, radio and telegram are no longer viable options for us. If we need reinforcements, someone must make the long trek to the next allied position, and then return again.

[This will consume one charge and summon several local fighter jets.]

[Without a Communications Tower, asking for reinforcements will take much longer.]

recipes.label: Call in Local Air Support?
recipes.startdescription:
My superiors have noted my achievements. As proof, the Soviet Air Force will come to support us and once again roar at the Germans.

[When friendly air forces on the field are weaker than enemy air forces, you can call in air support.]

recipes.label: Awaiting Reinforcements...
recipes.startdescription: Time does what it usually does, and passes. With luck, fresh allies are already en route.

recipes.label: Awaiting Reinforcements...
recipes.startdescription: Time does what it usually does, and passes. I can only hope that our messenger has gone unharried by the enemy or by the elements.

recipes.label: Arrived!
recipes.startdescription: More men to the cause; more meat to the slaughter.

recipes.label: Arrived!
recipes.startdescription: More men to the cause; more meat to the slaughter.

recipes.label: Enemy launches aerial combat!
recipes.startdescription:
Our forces are facing a deadly threat from the skies!

[In aerial combat, the attacker can only use fighters; the defender can additionally use bombers and anti-aircraft emplacements. However, if the defender wins, air superiority returns to neutral. If both sides have forces present, there is a chance that aircraft may run out of fuel and become exhausted, or be shot down and damaged.]
